source_review.notes: Checked all 12 structured references against current official Google SRE, AWS, W3C, OpenLineage, Apache Iceberg, NIST, OWASP, OpenTelemetry, and FinOps Foundation sources; every final URL returned HTTP 200. Verified scoped claims about production-readiness review, data-processing operations, analytics workload review, catalog/quality metadata, runtime/design lineage, transactional table state, cybersecurity/privacy risk outcomes, API threats, telemetry signals, and unit economics. Frameworks organize evidence but are not presented as end-to-end product certification.

evidence: Checked mandatory-gate conjunction, evidence tuple/chain, frozen scope tuple, failed/unknown counts, traceability graph, reconciliation sets, evidence age, and average-score proof notation plus balanced GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes gate status from prioritization score, product scope from evidence scope, graph traceability from truth, and recorded age from material-change invalidation.

evidence: Executed mandatory-product-review-gates and matched 12 mandatory gates, 10 passes, two failures, no unknowns, 0.833 pass rate, not-ready decision, and consumer-acceptance/recovery-drill blockers.
Recomputed the generalized example: 99 passes and one failure over 100 gates yields mean 0.99 while conjunction remains false.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic is exact under Boolean encoding; the text correctly states that real gate applicability and evidence truth require review rather than numeric scoring.

evidence: Verified that a conjunction of applicable mandatory gates requires failed and unknown counts both equal zero under the stated status policy.
Verified the mean counterexample (n-1)/n approaches one while a single false conjunct keeps readiness false.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proof is properly limited to mandatory Boolean gates; not-applicable, unknown, and explicitly authorized conditional policies are preserved separately.

evidence: Reviewed omitted sources, same-path totals, semantic/type mismatches, empty/late/duplicate/deleted/history cases, hot keys, source/vendor/control-plane loss, retries, backfills, rollback state, negative authorization, privacy propagation, incomplete lineage, stale owners, hidden consumers, and recovered old policy.

Reviewed high average with one critical failure, unknown and not-applicable misuse, permanent exceptions, tiny tests, configuration claims, no-incident inference, evidence expiry, and material-change invalidation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial review covers the source-to-consumer path and organizational, economic, lifecycle and recovery boundaries rather than only pipeline components.

evidence: Traced consumer outcomes, frozen identities, claim/evidence chains, independent reconciliation, consumer-visible SLOs, effective security/privacy, bounded replay/overload, representative capacity/economics, accountable ownership, mandatory gates and scoped exceptions through examples and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: No diagram, provider feature, job status, schema check, row count, dashboard, access listing, bill allocation, backup, quiet telemetry period, badge or issue-closure assertion is treated as broader proof than it supplies.

evidence: Reviewed the general one-failure construction proving a sub-unity mean threshold cannot guarantee conjunction.
Reviewed the omitted-tenant counterexample proving downstream component checks can all pass while end-to-end consumer completeness fails.
proof_review.notes: Both claims prove insufficiency at the stated scope and retain the useful roles of scores for prioritization and component checks for localization.

evidence: The average-score theorem is explicitly labeled a conditional claim with proof; component insufficiency is explicitly labeled and proved by counterexample.
The executable is labeled a deterministic conjunction illustration and disclaims real evidence truth, sufficiency, independence, freshness and applicability.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Logical implications, deterministic output, automated checks, empirical tests/observations, primary documentation, expert judgment and risk acceptance remain distinct.

evidence: Framework, standard, provider and project behavior is attributed to named primary sources and never called product certification.
Load/failure tests, SLOs, telemetry, incidents, lineage, reconciliation, costs, consumer acceptance and recovery drills are scoped by version, environment, workload, date and limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter consistently distinguishes planned from deployed, configured from effective, component from product, production observation from controlled test, unobserved from unused, and review receipt from permanent assurance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed end to end. The capstone coherently integrates consumer value/contracts, source semantics, transformation/lineage, independent quality, architecture/state/serving, SLOs/observability, security/privacy, change/lifecycle, capacity/economics, incident/recovery, ownership, review decisions and continuous validity.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed the charter, falsifiable product claim, twelve-step mechanism, gate statuses, evidence tuples, review-session workflow, findings/risks/exceptions, immutable receipt, re-review triggers, ten production examples and five detailed answers for operational usability.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed progression from one-page gate model through prerequisites, charter, consumers, flow, correctness, architecture, reliability, governance, change, economics, recovery, ownership, decision and continuous evidence; notation, two proofs, executable gate, 14 trade-offs, 36 misconceptions, ten examples and five complete answers synthesize the 100-module Data Engineering program. Cross-program links accurately connect API, Platform and Systems Engineering review disciplines.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
